notes: Stored edit with background-belief queries; replaces the verifier-rejected Declaration of Independence record, whose second world (Independence Hall stored only as the Declaration's place of adoption) clashed with the firm fact that the Constitution was also adopted there, and which shared its template (a building defined by an event) with history-replace-0002. Derivability very_unlikely: the volcano that destroyed Pompeii is stated everywhere and follows from nothing. The worlds split on how the AD 79 eruption is stored: under Vesuvius's name (w1: Herculaneum stays buried by Vesuvius, and the side fact that Pompeii and Herculaneum went in the same eruption gives way), or as the eruption that destroyed Pompeii (w2: it becomes Etna's, with Herculaneum). The two background queries are not independent: Herculaneum buried by Vesuvius in AD 79 while Vesuvius did not erupt in AD 79 contradicts itself, so there are two worlds, not four. Route dropped (step 3): 'destroyed by the volcano that overlooks the Bay of Naples' would put Etna in Campania. R1: the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius is undisputed (only its month is debated, and no query asks it). R2: no prompt names the volcano; the zh name 庞贝 gives nothing away. The near query (Italy) differs from the new answer and is no premise; Etna is also in Italy, so it stays the same in every world. The counterfactual is plausible (Etna is Italy's best-known active volcano, and the one Dolma hit for 'Etna destroyed Pompeii' reports a teacher saying so) and clearly false.
